checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the field element bounds check for public key coordinates using the correct field modulus p instead of subgroup order n?

reachability.notes: On secp256r1, p != n. Using n for field bounds would reject valid public key coordinates in [n, p), causing consensus failures.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the bounds check code for public key coordinate validation (qx, qy). 2. Verify the constant used is the field modulus p = 0xFFFFFFFF00000001000000000000000000000000FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF. 3. Confirm it is NOT using the subgroup order n = 0xFFFFFFFF00000000FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFBCE6FAADA7179E84F3B9CAC2FC632551. 4. Generate test vectors with coordinates in the range [n, p) and verify they are accepted. 5. Create a PoC with a valid public key where qx or qy falls in [n, p) range.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0016, Trust Boundary: tb-001, Invariant: EIP7951-SG004-INV-001

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does the P256VERIFY precompile reject inputs that are not exactly 160 bytes?

reachability.notes: Attacker controls calldata length and content. Short inputs could cause out-of-bounds reads; long inputs should be rejected per spec.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the input length validation logic in the precompile. 2. Test with inputs of length 0, 1, 159, 160, 161, 320 bytes. 3. Verify that only 160-byte inputs proceed to parsing. 4. Verify that non-160-byte inputs return empty output (not error). 5. Test short inputs (< 160) to ensure no out-of-bounds memory reads. 6. Check for crashes or panics with malformed input lengths.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0017, Trust Boundary: tb-001, Pre-condition: EIP7951-SG005-INV-001, Threat: stride-018

checklist.title: Verify Gas Sufficiency: Does the fixed 6900 gas cost cover worst-case execution time for all input patterns?

reachability.notes: Attacker can craft inputs to maximize computation time. Fixed 6900 gas means the attacker pays the same regardless of execution cost. If worst-case is significantly more expensive than average, this enables computational DoS.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify input patterns that trigger worst-case execution paths. 2. Test with edge-case values near 0 and n for modular inverse operations. 3. Test with degenerate elliptic curve point configurations. 4. Benchmark execution time for: average inputs, worst-case inputs, boundary values. 5. Compare execution time ratio between worst and average cases. 6. If ratio exceeds 2x, document as potential DoS vector. 7. Measure actual gas consumption vs 6900 fixed cost.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0018, Trust Boundary: tb-001/tb-002, Invariant: EIP7951-SG006-INV-003, Threat: stride-003. CONDITIONAL SCOPE: Requires further investigation - high-effort DoS may be out of scope per program rules.

checklist.title: Are modular inverse and elliptic curve operations in P256VERIFY implemented using constant-time algorithms?

reachability.notes: While EVM execution is deterministic, block processing time can vary. Timing side channels are less critical in the EVM context but could leak information to block producers observing execution traces.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Review the modular inverse implementation for conditional branches based on input values. 2. Review elliptic curve point multiplication for variable-time patterns. 3. Check for early-exit conditions that depend on secret values. 4. Analyze if the implementation uses constant-time primitives from the underlying crypto library. 5. Perform timing measurements with statistically significant sample sizes across different input values. 6. Document any timing variations > 1% between input classes.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0019, Trust Boundary: tb-001, Threat: stride-004. Low practical exploitability in EVM context.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does P256VERIFY return exactly 0x00...01 (32 bytes) for valid signatures and empty bytes for invalid signatures?

reachability.notes: This is the fundamental correctness property. If violated, either valid signatures are rejected (availability impact) or invalid signatures are accepted (integrity/confidentiality impact).

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Use NIST P-256 test vectors (CAVP ECDSA2VS) for known valid/invalid signatures. 2. Verify valid signatures return exactly 32 bytes: 0x0000...0001. 3. Verify invalid signatures return empty bytes (length 0). 4. Test edge cases: signature with r=0, s=0, r>=n, s>=n. 5. Test with public key at infinity, on curve but wrong point. 6. Verify no other return values are possible (not 0, not 2, not error codes). 7. Fuzz with random inputs and verify binary output space (success or empty).
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0020, Trust Boundary: tb-001/tb-003, Post-condition: EIP7951-SG001-INV-003, Threat: stride-001

checklist.title: Does get_blob_parameters correctly sort BLOB_SCHEDULE entries and return appropriate parameters for each epoch?

reachability.notes: While the function itself is not directly attacker-callable, its output determines blob limits applied to attacker-submitted blocks. An incorrect result would cause either under-validation (accepting excess blobs) or over-validation (rejecting valid blocks).

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Review the sorting logic for BLOB_SCHEDULE entries (must be descending by epoch). 2. Verify the lookup returns the first entry where entry.epoch <= queried_epoch. 3. Test with epochs: before any entry, exactly at entry epoch, between entries, far in future. 4. Test fallback behavior when no entry matches (should return ELECTRA defaults). 5. Verify ELECTRA_FORK_EPOCH and MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK_ELECTRA are used as defaults. 6. Create test cases for edge epochs around fork boundaries.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0021, Trust Boundary: tb-008, Post-condition: FULU-SG001-INV-004, Threat: stride-009

checklist.title: Are all epoch values in BLOB_SCHEDULE guaranteed to be unique to ensure deterministic parameter resolution?

reachability.notes: Configuration invariant. If duplicate epochs exist, the sort order becomes non-deterministic (depends on sort stability), causing different clients to potentially use different blob limits.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Extract all epoch values from the BLOB_SCHEDULE configuration. 2. Verify no duplicate epoch values exist in the schedule. 3. If duplicates exist, test sort behavior with the client's sorting algorithm. 4. Compare sort output with other client implementations for the same duplicate input. 5. Verify that validation/initialization code rejects duplicate epochs. 6. Check spec compliance for epoch uniqueness requirement.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0022, Trust Boundary: tb-008, Invariant: FULU-SG001-INV-001, Threat: stride-009

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does process_execution_payload correctly validate that payload.parent_hash matches state.latest_execution_payload_header.block_hash?

reachability.notes: A malicious proposer or P2P peer can submit blocks with arbitrary parent_hash values. Missing this check would break execution payload chaining.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate the parent_hash assertion in process_execution_payload. 2. Verify the check compares payload.parent_hash == state.latest_execution_payload_header.block_hash. 3. Test with a valid block (correct parent_hash) - should succeed. 4. Test with incorrect parent_hash (random hash) - must be rejected. 5. Test with parent_hash pointing to an older valid block - must be rejected. 6. Test with empty/zero parent_hash - must be rejected. 7. Verify rejection behavior: assert failure, not silent acceptance.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0025, Trust Boundary: tb-005/tb-006, Pre-condition: FULU-SG002-INV-001
